recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-32990; reconcile FHIR-55315 only as an independent later-change issue if it is assigned separately.
issue_request: FHIR-32990 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core AdverseEvent. It asked to clarify that AdverseEvent.actuality distinguishes actual events from near misses, and to add guidance that AllergyIntolerance should be used to capture an individual's propensity to an adverse reaction.
initial_application: Commit a3af5eb197a42ffa46032e8b62e3fc2f0f16069f, titled J#32990 Clarify AdverseEvent.actuality, added the J#32990 committee note, replaced the AdverseEvent.actuality definition with the near-miss wording, and added the AllergyIntolerance propensity comment in source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps AdverseEvent in current build scope. Later Applied issue FHIR-55315 changed the same element by adding an unknown code and a strongly discouraged legacy-data note, but preserved the FHIR-32990 definition and AllergyIntolerance guidance. The AdverseEvent introduction also describes potential adverse events as near misses and keeps propensity/risk concepts directed to more specific resources. Community searches found one Patient Care WGM minutes page referencing FHIR-32990 with AdverseEvent change requests and no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current structure definition already implements the FHIR-32990 resolution, and additional edits would either duplicate existing guidance or risk disturbing the later FHIR-55315 clarification.
